Use the model above to calculate the value of $4÷\frac{5}{6}.$
question.worked_solution:
To calculate $4÷\frac{5}{6}$, we first need to divide each of the $4$ wholes into $6$ equal parts.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/90771544aed1e49a45f857d5fe041476a0f8e6130c87466f6853e76468f1fa14.png)

 

Next, we break this into groups of $5$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/2343c93c7c92c4510b5f19b2cd3d9e2221da6f69996009ac4e6b669bbcac5278.png)

 

Note the following: 

- We got $\boxed{\text{4}}$ full groups.

- There are $4$ pieces left over out of a possible group of $5.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{4}{5}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
4÷\frac{5}{6}=\boxed{\text{4}}\,\frac{4}{5}.
$$
